chapter_title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

items.title: Constructing an Equilateral Triangle
items.explanation: An equilateral triangle is formed when all three sides are of equal length. To construct a triangle with side lengths of 4 cm, follow these steps: First, draw a base AB of 4 cm. Using a compass, place the needle at A and mark an arc with a radius of 4 cm. Then, place the needle at B and mark another arc with a radius of 4 cm. The point where these two arcs intersect is vertex C. Joining AC and BC creates the equilateral triangle ABC.

items.title: Constructing a Triangle from Three Side Lengths
items.explanation: To construct a triangle with specific side lengths (e.g., 4 cm, 5 cm, and 6 cm), choose one side as the base. For instance, if AB is the base of 4 cm, use a compass to draw an arc centered at A with a radius equal to the second side length (5 cm). Then, from point B, draw another arc with a radius equal to the third side length (6 cm). The intersection point of these two arcs is vertex C. Joining AC and BC completes the triangle.
